newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wills wins first round of brand dispute.
newsitem.headline: Wills wins first round of brand dispute.

text.p: The Australian subsidiary of cigarette manufacturer B.A.T. Industries Plc said on Wednesday it had won the first stage of a branding dispute with a Philip Morris Inc -backed rival.

W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd said after the start of Federal Court proceedings Philip Morris Australia had agreed not to "sell, offer for sale or promote" value brand Summit in its current packaging, pending a further hearing.
Wills launched the proceedings on Monday, accusing Philip Morris Australia of misleading and deceptive conduct.
Wills said Philip Morris had planned to launch its Summit brand packaged almost identically in terms of colour, lettering and imagery to Wills' Horizon value brand.
A spokeswoman for Philip Morris said the company had agreed not to launch the Summit brand before June 11 but was seeking an early resolution.
"We are currently seeking a date for the matter to be heard, obviously as soon as possible, and will vigorously defend the action," Philip Morris corporate affairs manager Nerida White told Reuters.

Wills said Philip Morris had earlier told the court it had 47 million Summit cigarettes worth about A$900,000 ahead of a planned June 16 launch which would have to sit idle until the matter was resolved.
"Wills is committed to defending Horizon against unwarranted attack," Wills corporate affairs head Suzanne Povey said in a statement.
Povey described Horizon as "the fastest growing cigarette brand this decade".
Wills is 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc.
